problem: The chapter defines K_H = 1/(n q t) and calls it 'the Hall coefficient in m²/C'. Standard textbooks define the Hall coefficient as R_H = 1/(n q), with units m³/C. The quantity 1/(n q t) is a sensitivity (it depends on plate thickness), not the Hall coefficient, so a student writing the textbook definition in the exam will lose marks.
fix: Keep V_H = K_H I B but call K_H = 1/(n q t) the Hall sensitivity (current-related sensitivity), units V/(A·T) or m²/C, because V_H = I B/(n q t). Then state separately: the Hall coefficient is R_H = 1/(n q) in m³/C, and for a plate of thickness t, V_H = R_H I B / t.

problem: 'Hall sensors are used for cam and crank position, wheel speed, pedal position and gear selection. They need a supply and give a digital signal' — pedal position normally uses a linear (analog output) Hall sensor, so 'digital signal' contradicts the pedal example given in the same sentence.
fix: Say: 'Most are digital switches; linear Hall versions give an analog voltage that is used for pedal and throttle position.'

problem: The column header 'Dirt' with values High / Medium / Low can be read either as dirt tolerance or as dirt sensitivity. A student could read 'VR: High' as 'VR is badly affected by dirt', the opposite of what the text says.
fix: Rename the column 'Dirt tolerance' and note 'High = works despite dirt'. Values stay: VR high, Hall medium, optical low.
